stem: During handover, a registrar says, “This child needs a FaCS report today”; what is the best interpretation of that instruction?

options.text: Make an immediate report to the Child Protection Helpline for risk of significant harm
Call the Child Wellbeing Unit for advice during office hours because all FaCS reports go there first
Arrange only a forensic medical assessment with the Child Protection Unit
Complete a school-based welfare referral rather than a statutory child protection report
Continue to monitor and support, because a FaCS report is not a formal notification

explanation: A FaCS report means an immediate report to the Child Protection Helpline for risk of significant harm. It is another term for a Child Protection Report or ROSH report.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: A FaCS report is another term for a Child Protection Report or risk of significant harm report, and it is made to the Child Protection Helpline.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a FaCS report is the statutory child protection report made to the Child Protection Helpline when there is risk of significant harm.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the Child Wellbeing Unit is not the required pathway for a FaCS report and does not replace the statutory helpline report.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a forensic medical assessment is a separate clinical action and is not the same as making a FaCS report.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a FaCS report refers to a statutory child protection report, not a school-based welfare referral.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a FaCS report is a formal notification pathway, not a reason to simply monitor the child without reporting.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
